newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: LC Development buys Australian vineyard.
newsitem.headline: LC Development buys Australian vineyard.

text.p: LC Development Ltd, the property arm of Lum Chang Holdings, said on Thursday it was buying a Western Australian vineyard and winery for a total of A$2.15 million.

The purchase of the 208-acre Chittering Estate Vineyard and Winery near Perth was made through a joint venture with Jendami Pty Ltd, an Australian incorporated company. The seller was Kondil Nominees Pty Ltd, a trustee of the T.G. Kailis Family Discretionary Trust of RC Slater.
An LC Development statement said the vineyard cost A$900,000 while the winery business cost A$1.25 million.
LC Development would hold a 75 percent stake in the venture and Jendami the remainder.
Jendami would manage the business for an annual fee of A$50,000, the statement said.
Chittering Estate's sales in fiscal year 1996 were about S$970,000, it added.
The completion of the sale is subject to obtaining a liquor licence within 90 days from January 24.
LC Development said the acquisition was not expected to have a significant impact on its earnings for the its fiscal year ending June 30, 1997.
